claim: Make sure your domain name registrar uses the name servers of your Amazon Route 53 hosted zone; if not, Amazon Route 53 is not authoritative for queries to your domain.
question: Why might Route 53 not be authoritative for a domain even though a hosted zone exists?

values.display: will not be authoritative for queries to your domain

evidence.quote: You should also make sure that your domain name registrar is using the name servers in your Amazon Route 53 hosted zone.
If not, Amazon Route 53 will not be authoritative for queries to your domain.

claim: An alias record can map the zone apex to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment DNS name.
question: Can the zone apex point at an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment?

values.display: zone apex (example.com) DNS name to your AWS Elastic Beanstalk DNS name

evidence.quote: Amazon Route 53 offers a special type of record called an ‘Alias’ record that lets you map your zone apex (example.com) DNS name to your AWS Elastic Beanstalk DNS name (i.e. example.elasticbeanstalk.com).

claim: There is no additional charge for queries to alias records mapped to Elastic Beanstalk environments, API Gateways or VPC endpoints.
question: Is there a charge for Route 53 queries to alias records that point at API Gateway, Elastic Beanstalk or VPC endpoints?

values.display: no additional charge for queries to Alias records

qualifiers.scope: alias records mapped to AWS resources

evidence.quote: Queries to Alias records that are mapped to AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments are free.
There is no additional charge for queries to Alias records that are mapped to Amazon API Gateways.
There is no additional charge for queries to Alias records that are mapped to Amazon VPC endpoints.

claim: The IP addresses of CloudFront endpoints vary with the end user's location and can change at any time, so you map a name to the distribution's DNS name with an alias record.
question: Why do you point at a CloudFront distribution by DNS name instead of by IP address?

values.display: vary based on your end user’s location

evidence.quote: IP addresses associated with Amazon CloudFront endpoints vary based on your end user’s location (in order to direct the end user to the nearest CloudFront edge location) and can change at any time due to scaling up, scaling down, or software updates.

claim: You can manage private IP addresses within VPCs by using the Private DNS feature of Amazon Route 53.
question: Can Route 53 manage an organization's private IP addresses?

values.display: manage private IP addresses within Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs)

evidence.quote: Yes, you can manage private IP addresses within Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) using Amazon Route 53’s Private DNS feature.

claim: You can combine Geo DNS with other routing types, such as Latency Based Routing and DNS Failover, to build low-latency and fault-tolerant architectures.
question: Can geolocation routing be combined with latency routing or failover?

values.display: combine Geo DNS with other routing types

evidence.quote: You can also combine Geo DNS with other routing types, such as Latency Based Routing and DNS Failover, to enable a variety of low-latency and fault-tolerant architectures.

claim: You can view the current status of a health check and details on why it failed in the Amazon Route 53 console and through the API.
question: How do you see the status of a Route 53 health check?

values.display: console and via the Route 53 API

evidence.quote: You can view the current status of a health check, as well as details on why it has failed, in the Amazon Route 53 console and via the Route 53 API.

claim: Route 53 VPC Resolver on Outposts resolves DNS queries locally on AWS Outposts racks, stores DNS responses there, and keeps DNS resolution going during network disconnects to the parent AWS Region.
question: What does Route 53 VPC Resolver on Outposts provide?

values.display: continued DNS resolution for your applications even during unexpected network disconnects

qualifiers.condition: when Route 53 VPC Resolver is enabled on Outposts

evidence.quote: When you enable Route 53 VPC Resolver on Outposts, Route 53 automatically stores DNS responses on Outposts racks and provides continued DNS resolution for your applications even during unexpected network disconnects to the parent AWS Region.

claim: Amazon Route 53 VPC Resolver supports the DNS over HTTPS (DoH) protocol for both inbound and outbound Resolver endpoints.
question: Do Route 53 Resolver endpoints support DNS over HTTPS?

evidence.quote: Yes, Amazon Route 53 VPC Resolver supports using the DNS over HTTPS (DoH) protocol for both inbound and outbound resolver endpoints.
